units: metres, kilograms, newtons; +X left, +Y up, +Z forward, as AC and glTF
derived_note: Every shape here is a convex hull of geometry AC only draws. AC states no collision for it and no mass for anything, so the masses and break loads come from the class table, not the content.

class_table.name: lamp_column
class_table.note: steel lighting column with its head and arm; frangible at the base plate

class_table.name: bollard_post
class_table.note: bollard, short post, meter stand: a solid section rather than a tube, so the hull is nearly all metal and the effective density is high

class_table.name: pole_sign
class_table.note: sign or parking-meter post: thin tube, light, goes over easily

class_table.name: street_furniture
class_table.note: mailbox, litter bin, hydrant, meter cabinet: bolted down, not cast in

class_table.name: low_furniture
class_table.note: bollard, kerb box, small planter: low enough to be climbed as much as hit

class_table.name: bench_barrier
class_table.note: bench, railing run, light barrier: moves, but takes a real hit to move

class_table.name: heavy_structure
class_table.note: concrete plinth, retaining wall, stair block: too much of it to shift, so it stays static and the mass is reported for information only

buildings.carriageway_note: a hull that contains a drivable point was cut until it did not; what is left is reported per building as blocks_road, and is geometry that genuinely sits over the road

props.items_note: everything needed to build a body, so a loader never has to read node extras: inertia_kgm2 and anchor are null on a static body and set on every dynamic one. hulls names the mesh of each convex piece, in the same order as the body's children
